analysis.one_liner: BPCL is a Government of India-owned oil refiner and fuel marketer that turns crude oil into petrol, diesel and LPG, and sells it through one of India's largest retail networks.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026) results were declared on 23 Oct 2026: consolidated net profit fell 21% YoY to ₹4,863 crore even as revenue jumped nearly 30% to ₹1,49,080 crore, as marketing margins on petrol, diesel and LPG were squeezed by higher crude costs that pump prices did not fully track. This follows a rare net loss of ₹1,873 crore in Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026). Management also set up a wholly-owned subsidiary for the proposed Ramayapatnam greenfield refinery/petrochemical project and flagged capex rising sharply to ₹40,000-45,000 crore a year in FY28-29, from roughly ₹25,000 crore planned for FY27.
analysis.plain_terms: BPCL buys crude oil, refines it, and sells fuel to the public - its profit depends less on how much it sells and more on the gap between what crude costs and what it's allowed to charge at the pump. That gap shrank this quarter because crude got pricier while retail fuel prices stayed put, which is why profit fell even as revenue jumped nearly 30%. The business swung from a ₹1,873 crore loss in June 2026 to a ₹4,863 crore profit in September 2026 - a reminder of how volatile quarterly earnings are here. The real tension: BPCL looks cheap on paper (P/E near 9, ROE near 29%) but a chunk of that profitability depends on government fuel-pricing decisions it doesn't control.
analysis.quarters: Quarterly profit has swung sharply: ₹7,188 crore (Q3 FY26, Dec'25) to ₹5,625 crore (Q4 FY26, Mar'26) to a net loss of ₹1,873 crore (Q1 FY27, Jun'26, operating loss ₹4,055 crore) to ₹4,863 crore (Q2 FY27, Sep'26). The ~30% YoY revenue jump in Q2 FY27 mostly reflects higher crude-linked price levels, not higher volumes - domestic sales were roughly flat (13.47 MMT vs 13.62 MMT in Q1). Management cited a gross refining margin of $32.53/bbl before adjusting for the Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED), falling to about $14/bbl after - headline GRM figures here are not comparable without checking that adjustment. Suppressed marketing margins on petrol, diesel and LPG were called out as the main drag.
analysis.performance_read: Over 5 years the stock returned 67.45% versus Nifty's 25.03% and peer IOC's 101.99%; over 3 years it returned 95.68% versus Nifty's 18.95% and IOC's 74.45%. The stock is down 25.6% from its 9 Feb 2026 peak of ₹388.30. This fall is not a corporate-action artifact - BPCL has had five stock splits since 2000 (2000, 2012, 2016, 2017, 2024) but no demerger or spin-off, so the price series already reflects those splits and the drawdown is a genuine price move, not an optical one.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 9x and price-to-book of about 1.25x (price ₹289 vs book value ₹234), BPCL looks statistically cheap against a sector median P/E in the mid-teens. Why it's cheap: oil marketing companies are structurally capped since the government effectively controls retail fuel pricing, so profit depends on political pass-through decisions as much as operating efficiency - the Q1 FY27 loss is exactly the kind of risk the market is discounting. Whether that discount is large enough depends on whether marketing margins normalise as crude eases, which is not verified here.
analysis.growth_read: Revenue growth is not a reliable volume signal this quarter - the ~30% YoY jump coincided with roughly flat sales volumes (13.47 MMT vs 13.62 MMT), making it price/crude-cost-led rather than demand-led. On margins, the business moved the wrong way: EBITDA and net profit both fell YoY despite the revenue jump, i.e. margin compression, not margin-led growth. Underlying volume trends beyond FY26's cited 27.27% market share and 25,323 outlets are not verified in this review.
analysis.health_read: Reported profitability looks strong - ROE of about 28.8% (3-year average 28.6%) and ROCE of about 25.6% - and FY26 free cash flow was reported at ₹31,476 crore, suggesting profits converted to cash in a normal year. Total debt stood at about ₹54,424 crore as of March 2026. The real risk is not balance-sheet health but business/regulatory risk: a single quarter of unfavourable crude-to-retail-price timing wiped out profit entirely in Q1 FY27, and the jump in planned capex to ₹40,000-45,000 crore a year for FY28-29 (from ~₹25,000 crore for FY27) will need funding without letting leverage balloon - worth re-checking each quarter.
analysis.ownership_read: The Government of India is the promoter with a 52.98% stake, unchanged in the September 2026 quarter, and promoter pledging is 0% - expected for a state-owned enterprise rather than a special sign of comfort. Combined FII+DII ownership is a little below 39%, with FIIs trimming slightly (16.84% to 16.66%) and mutual funds also paring back (9.56% to 9.13%), while other DII holdings rose. No marquee individual investor shows up on the register based on available data.
strengths: ROE of ~28.8% and ROCE of ~25.6% remain well above typical refining-sector benchmarks even after a weak quarter
Dividend yield of about 6.05% (TTM dividend ₹17.50), among the higher payouts in the large-cap PSU space
Refinery utilisation ran at 117% of nameplate capacity in Q2 FY27, showing no capacity constraint on refining
Zero promoter pledging and a stable 52.98% government stake removes a common governance risk seen at leveraged corporates
watchpoints: Marketing margins on fuel are set administratively, not purely by the market - Q1 FY27's ₹1,873 crore loss shows how quickly that turns negative when crude rises and pump prices don't follow
Capex plans rise sharply to ₹40,000-45,000 crore a year in FY28-29 from roughly ₹25,000 crore for FY27, needing funding without materially raising the ₹54,424 crore (Mar 2026) debt load
Stock is down 25.6% from its February 2026 peak, and profit swung from a loss to a ₹4,863 crore profit within one quarter, making near-term earnings hard to forecast

GRM figures need scrutiny - the quarter's $32.53/bbl refining margin falls to roughly $14/bbl after adjusting for the Special Additional Excise Duty, so headline numbers aren't automatically comparable across quarters
analysis.one_thing: Whether government-administered retail fuel prices are allowed to catch up with crude costs over the next 1-2 quarters - that policy decision determines whether marketing margins and reported profit recover from the Q1 FY27 loss or stay compressed.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly financials, valuation ratios, shareholding and pledge data were cross-checked against Screener.in's consolidated figures, consistent with Business Standard's reporting of the Q2 FY27 consolidated net profit of ₹4,863 crore and ~30% revenue growth. One source reported a slightly different standalone net profit (₹4,993 crore) for the same quarter; that figure was set aside in favour of the consolidated number used throughout. A GuruFocus ROE figure of -7.48% was inconsistent with Screener's 28.8% and was discarded as likely stale or mismatched. FY26 market share, outlet count and FY28-29 capex guidance are management-cited figures from the earnings call and have not been independently verified beyond that source.
